## Body

**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `83bb002b5751c40d334029d541ce3a8d65a05094`.

Full cost review against main `246f9587c2f62f20f8767409f495c393dda6bea0`. Earlier #168 heads were held; no earlier performance verdict is being carried forward.

**No new loop, timer, background poll or executable site.** Work is driven by verb calls. Existing counted sites are reused: `gh.delivered`, `git.community`, `ddocs.community` and `tmux.rename-window`. The launch helpers and spawn-site guard are unchanged. Git/tmux use the shared cached executable resolver; gh/ddocs retain their startup-resolved absolute paths. Existing missing/disappearing-executable behavior, Git hooks and delivery descendants are not made process-free.

**One commit is not one Git launch.** Traced `CommunityWriter::write_with` through `root::resolve` and `write_serialised`: a normal successful write launches Git **seven times**: three root-resolution commands, status, add, commit, and rev-parse HEAD. ddocs validate and build add **two launches per changed DD document**, including any holders documents carrying pending close-ends. Markdown ROUTES adds no ddocs launch.

| Verb/path | Normal direct community Git calls | Other relevant cost |
|---|---|---|
| `delivered`, no selected holding or missing merge time | 0 | Existing one gh call; store/PR processing remains |
| `delivered`, selected targets all unmatched under the writer lock | 3 | Root resolution occurs before the build refuses; zero commits is not zero launches |
| `delivered`, releases land | 7 | One gh call, 2D ddocs calls, up to U rename invocations |
| `release --batch` of N valid holdings | 7, versus 7N single-release writer calls | 2D ddocs calls, up to U rename invocations |
| Assign/release/lineage, single or existing batch | 7 per successful writer commit, unchanged | Existing per-document and delivery/window work remains |
| Close's holding ends | 7 per affected project, unchanged | One commit per project, not one across every project |

Here D is the number of DD documents actually written, including flushed pending ends; U is the number of distinct released non-tombstoned seats considered for window updates. Counts exclude inherited Git hooks, resolver retries and notification/delivery work. Standard index-lock handling can retry add and commit four additional times each; failed staged writes can also launch a rollback reset. No normal-path Git call is multiplied by the batch's holding count.

**Delivered selection and batch scaling:** `finished_by` reads all open and closed assignment rows for the project, then filters in memory, O(A) retained project holdings. If targets remain, `release_many` reads the project's assignments again to select pending ends. Merge time rides the existing gh JSON read; the exact `from` pin is checked against holders documents already read under the writer lock, with no additional query or process.

The batch writes whole histories for distinct affected roles, and indexes N ends in one existing store transaction (plus pending-end indexing when needed). Duplicate detection scans target prefixes, O(N²); target matching scans the corresponding holder histories. Window processing sorts/deduplicates seats, then scans receipts for each seat's earliest ended holding, O(U*N), with one registry lookup and one open-holdings read per eligible seat. It makes at most one rename invocation per seat, not per released holding. Input, history and output bytes still scale; batching is not constant total work.

**P168-N001, budget qualifications:** ROUTES checking is in-process, but not a cheap timestamp check. `regenerate` reads/parses every role document once, clones the set, builds both before/after tables, diffs them and renders the candidate Markdown even when current. Deduplication, path-overlap checks and table diff have quadratic scope-row work, with overlap output potentially quadratic too. This runs under the writer lock once per successful build that has not already regenerated routes. The shared `commit_keeping` also covers **output, memory and external writes**, not just the holdings verbs listed in the PR table. A current ROUTES file is not rewritten, but the recomputation still occurs. Scope-changing add/edit/retire/merge avoid a second regeneration through `built.routes`.

F90 adds one query **per qualifying role per directory view**, plus its schema check, not one query across all roles. The trigger counts live open holding rows. Its forced index is `(project, state, created_at)`: the query searches the project's delivered-request partition, then filters role/answer/holder and groups by holder. The passing EXPLAIN test proves an indexed SEARCH, not a role-specific or constant-work lookup; K qualifying roles can each examine that partition. No new view timer or process was added.

**CI:** [42428276067](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42428276067) succeeds at this exact SHA, including Rust lint/test and Node 22/24 checks. Downloaded JUnit records **2,194 executed cases, zero failures/errors/skips**, including **89 directory HTTP cases**, **8 claims HTTP cases**, all six spawn guards, the F90 query-plan case and renderer cases. Read the new batch/replay/pin tests: real Git commit-count assertions establish one commit for several releases and unchanged HEAD on rerun; the deterministic selection/reassignment interleaving preserves the newer holding. These tests use fake ddocs/tmux/gh seams, so they do not measure production child-launch counts or latency. Delivers `42428276053` succeeds; its cancelled duplicate is not proof.
